a: Rust is a systems language focused on safety, speed, and concurrency without a garbage collector.
Ownership means each value has one owner; when the owner goes out of scope, the value is dropped.
Borrowing lets you reference data without taking ownership, with either shared or mutable borrows.
Lifetimes ensure references remain valid for as long as needed.
Cargo is Rust's build system and package manager.
Result<T, E> represents success (Ok) or failure (Err) without exceptions.
Option<T> is Some(value) or None — Rust's null-safe optional.
match is exhaustive pattern matching for enums and other types.
Traits define shared behavior, similar to interfaces.
async/await in Rust uses futures; runtimes like Tokio execute them.
